The decisions of the referee, and all other match officials, must always be respected.</p><p>The referee may not change a restart decision on realising that it is incorrect or on the advice of another match official if play has restarted or the referee has signalled the end of the first or second half (including extra time) and left the field of play or abandoned the match. implementation</added> requirements as set out in <added>the VAR Handbook</added>, and has received written permission from FIFA.</p><p>The referee may be assisted by a video assistant referee (VAR) only in the event of a ‘clear and obvious error’ or ‘serious missed incident’ in relation to:</p><ul><li><p>goal/no goal</p></li></ul><ul><li><p>penalty/no penalty</p></li></ul><ul><li><p><explanation changed immediately and without delaying the restart (competition option)</addedexplanation></explanation></p></li></ul><p>The assistance from the video assistant referee (VAR) will relate to using replay(s) of the incident. The referee will make the final decision which may be based solely on the information from the VAR and/or the referee reviewing the replay footage directly (‘on-field review’).</p><p>Except for a ‘serious missed incident’, the referee (and where relevant other ‘on-field’ match officials) must always make a decision (including a decision not to penalise a potential offence); this decision does not change unless it is a ‘clear and obvious error’.</p><h3>Reviews after play has restarted</h3><p>If play has stopped and restarted, the referee may only undertake a ‘review’, and take the appropriate disciplinary sanction, for mistaken identity or for a potential sending-off offence relating to violent conduct, spitting, biting or extremely offensive, insulting and/or abusive action(s).</p></div></div></div></div><div></div></div></article></div><div class="bg-white overflow-hidden"><article id="referees-equipment" class="

  "><button type="button" class=""><span class="flex items-start py-0.5"><span class="mr-3 leading-none w-8 flex-shrink-0">5<!-- -->.<!-- -->7<!-- --> </span><span> </span><span class="leading-none">Liability of match officials</span></span></button></h2><div class="overflow-hidden laws-accordion-content" style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="LawSection__DynamicHtmlStyles-sc-1eqe7em-0 fmspFc"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ text-left "><div><p>A referee or other match official is not held liable for:</p> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>any kind of injury suffered by a player, official or spectator</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>any damage to property of any kind</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>any other loss suffered by any individual, club, company, association or other body, which is due or which may be due to any decision taken under the terms of the Laws of the Game or in respect of the normal procedures required to hold, play and control a match</p></li> 
</ul> 
<p>Such decisions may include a decision:</p> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>that the condition of the field of play or its surrounds or that the weather conditions are such as to allow or not to allow a match to take place</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>to abandon a match for whatever reason</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>as to the suitability of the field equipment and ball used during a match</p></li> 
</ul>

 <li><p>to stop or not to stop a match due to spectator interference or any problem in spectator areas</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>to stop or not to stop play to allow an injured player to be removed from the field of play for treatment</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>to require an injured player to be removed from the field of play for treatment</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>to allow or not to allow a player to wear certain clothing or equipment</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>where the referee has the authority, to allow or not to allow any persons (including team or stadium officials, security officers, photographers or other media representatives) to be present in the vicinity of the field of play</p></li> 
</ul> 
<ul> 
 <li><p>any other decision taken in accordance with the Laws of the Game or in conformity with their duties under the terms of FIFA, confederation, national football association or competition rules or regulations under which the match is played</p></li> 
</ul></div></div></div></div><div></div></div></article></div></div><div class="bg-white"><div class="Highlight__StyledHighlight-sc-1mykw48-0 bmcvZQ container overflow-auto"><h3 class="text-start font-thin text-deepDarkBlue tracking-wider text-3xl mb-5 sm:text-4xl md:text-5xl md:-ml-6 -ml-2 mt-14"><span class="TextHightlight__TextDecoration-j8wgf4-0 dhxRXS  block w-full"><span class="whitespace-pre-line text-left leading-tight">FAQs</span></span></h3></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>While taking a throw-in, a player holds the ball over the head and then drops it onto the ground inside the field of play. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Law 15 clearly states that the thrower must ‘throw’ the ball. If the ball is ‘dropped’ and not thrown, the throw-in is not taken correctly. In this case, the opposing team will take the throw-in, unless they gain possession of the ball and the referee applies the advantage when allowing play to continue is of greater benefit to them than awarding a throw-in.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player lifts one foot off the ground while taking a throw-in and the ball enters the field of play. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The throw-in is retaken by the opposing team because the Laws of the Game require the thrower to have part of both feet on/touching the ground (on or behind the touchline) at the moment of delivering the ball. However, if the opponents gain possession of the ball, the referee may apply the advantage if this is of greater benefit than awarding them the throw-in.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>What is the referee’s decision if a throw-in is not taken correctly?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>If the ball did not directly enter the field of play, the throw-in is retaken by the same team. If the ball entered the field of play, the opposing team takes the throw-in, unless the referee applies the advantage (it is only possible if the ball came into play and the opposing team will benefit from allowing play to continue, e.g. they gained possession of the ball).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>An attacking player (Team A) kicks the ball which then accidentally touches a hand/arm of their team-mate (Team A). The referee stops play, but wrongly decides that the handball offence was committed by a defending player (Team B), who is punished with a yellow card (YC) and a direct free kick to Team A. May the video assistant referee (VAR) inform the referee that the player from the non-offending team was cautioned?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>A YC which is not a second YC can be reviewed to identify the player who committed the handball offence that was penalised. In this case, the YC for the defender is cancelled and play is restarted with a direct free kick to Team B.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>An attacker challenges a defender, who falls to the ground in the middle of the field and pretends to have been fouled, despite there being no contact. The referee stops play, awards a free kick for the defender’s team and shows a yellow card (YC) to the attacker, which is their second YC in the match and results in a red card (RC). May the video assistant referee (VAR) inform the referee about a ‘clear and obvious error’ so that the incident is reviewed?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Yes, the VAR can assist the referee in relation to a clearly incorrect second YC. After the referee reviews the replay footage, the second YC and the subsequent RC for the attacker are cancelled. The ball goes to an opposing player who scores a goal. As an opponent then enters the penalty area and runs towards the ball, the goalkeeper kicks the ball again (before it has touched any other player). This second touch prevents the opponent from gaining control of the ball, denying them an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO); however, the ball rebounds off the opponent’s leg and goes into the goal. As the injury is not the result of an offence, the referee restarts play with a dropped ball to a player of the attacking team at the position of the ball when play was stopped.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>The referee stops play and awards a penalty kick because a defender recklessly tackles an attacker inside the defender’s penalty area. The attacker goes down and appears to be seriously injured. As the injury results from a physical offence for which the opponent is cautioned, the attacker may stay on the field of play after the assessment/treatment.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player (Team A) commits a brutal tackle while challenging an opponent (Team B) for the ball. The Team B player may stay on the field after the assessment/treatment.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player (Team A) committed a foul challenge against an opponent (Team B) in a manner considered by the referee to be reckless. The Team A player is cautioned (yellow card), must leave the field of play and remain off it until play has restarted and one minute has elapsed. Is the player required to leave the field if they are able to continue after the initial assessment/treatment?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The player can remain on the field of play and take the free kick if the injury results from a physical offence for which the opponent is cautioned (yellow card) or sent off (red card). Otherwise, the player must leave the field of play and may only re-enter one minute after play has restarted.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player takes a free kick while the ball is moving and attempts to make a short pass to a team-mate. What should the referee decide?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Although the ball must be stationary when a free kick is taken, the referee may apply the advantage if allowing play to continue is of greater benefit to the opposing team than ordering a retake.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player takes a throw-in from the wrong position and throws the ball onto the field of play. What should the referee do if the opposing team gains possession of the ball?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Although the ball is not thrown from the point where it left the field of play, as the ball entered the field of play, the referee may apply the advantage if allowing play to continue is of greater benefit to the opposing team than awarding a throw-in.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>At the moment of delivering the ball at a throw-in, a player has one foot outside the field of play and the other foot fully inside the field (not touching the touchline). What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>According to Law 15, the thrower must have part of each foot on the touchline or on the ground outside the touchline. Although the throw-in was not taken correctly, as the ball came into play, the referee may apply advantage and allow play to continue if this benefits the opposing team.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender recklessly challenges an attacker for the ball inside the defender’s penalty area and this foul denies the opponent an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO). What is the sanction if the referee awards a penalty kick?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The defender committed two offences listed in Law 12 under ‘Cautions for unsporting behaviour’:</p><ul><li><p>a direct free kick offence committed in a reckless manner</p></li><li><p>a DOGSO offence which was a challenge for the ball and resulted in a penalty kick</p></li></ul><p>When more than one offence occurs at the same time, the referee punishes the more serious offence. As both offences are punishable with a yellow card, a yellow card is shown for the reckless challenge, as its physical severity is more serious than the ‘tactical’ DOGSO offence.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender recklessly tackles an attacker outside the penalty area and this foul denies the opponent an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO). What is the correct decision if the advantage is not applied?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee stops play and awards a direct free kick. When two offences are committed at the same time, the more serious offence is punished, so the defender receives a red card for the DOGSO offence rather than a yellow card for the reckless foul.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player from Team A is carelessly tackled by an opponent from Team B in the middle of the field. What is the decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee waited a few seconds to allow a possible advantage to develop. As Team A did not benefit from the decision to continue play, the referee returns to the original offence and awards a direct free kick to Team A from the position where the tackle occurred.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>After the referee awards a free kick against Team A, the captain approaches the referee and shows dissent while the referee is explaining the decision. What action can be taken against the captain?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Referees’ decisions must always be respected and a team captain can be punished for dissent, just like any other player. Therefore, if a captain fails to interact with the referee in a respectful manner, a caution (yellow card) is issued.</p><p></p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>After the first half has ended, the referee sees a player striking an opponent in the tunnel on the way to the dressing rooms. What is the correct procedure?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee has the power to show cards during the half-time interval, even if the offence occurs off the field of play. The player is shown a red card for violent conduct, takes no further part in the match, and cannot be replaced. Since the card is shown off the field, the referee must inform both teams and, where appropriate, ensure an announcement is made to the spectators before the second half begins.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>After the final whistle has been blown, a player argues with the referee on the field of play and clearly shows dissent verbally, without attempting to touch the referee. What action can be taken against the player?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee has the authority to take disciplinary action until leaving the field of play. Even though the match has ended, an appropriate card may still be shown if it helps manage the situation or calm the player. Verbal dissent is punished with a caution (yellow card), unless the words are offensive, insulting, or abusive (red card). Regardless of whether the card is shown or not, the referee must report the offence to the appropriate authorities.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player is cautioned (shown a yellow card, YC) for unsporting behaviour between the toss of a coin and the kick-off. What is the correct procedure if the same player receives another YC during a match?
</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee has the power to show red and yellow cards from the moment they enter the field at the start of the match. Therefore, a caution (YC) issued between the coin toss and the kick-off is carried into the match, and if they receive a second YC during the match the player is sent off (shown a red card).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender and an attacker jump for a header in the middle of the field and collide in the air while competing legally for the ball (neither of them touches it). After that, both players fall to the ground and appear to be seriously injured so the referee stops play to allow the players to be assessed/treated accordingly. How will play be restarted if the ball was outside the penalty area when play was stopped?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Play will be restarted with a dropped ball (as outlined in Law 8).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>While the ball is in play, a spectator throws a bottle onto the field towards a player who is running with the ball, close to the touchline. The player stops running to avoid the bottle. What is the referee’s decision?  </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The object interfered with play so the referee stops a match and has the bottle removed from the field. If the match is not suspended or abandoned for safety reasons, play restarts with a dropped ball (as outlined in Law 8).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>After the first half has ended, a player argues with the referee, verbally protesting against a referee’s decision made earlier in the match. This occurs while both the player and referee are outside the field of play, heading towards the tunnel. What is the correct procedure in this situation?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>According to Law 5, the referee has the power to show cards during the half-time interval. Therefore, the player must be cautioned (yellow card) for dissent. If the card is shown off the field of play, the referee must inform both teams and, where appropriate, ensure that an announcement is made to spectators before the second half begins.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender recklessly tackles an attacker. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee stops play and awards a direct free kick from the position of the shirt-pulling offence. The defender is therefore shown two yellow cards, followed by a red card, and is sent off.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender from Team A recklessly tackles an opponent near the touchline and thus stops a promising attack by Team B. What is the correct restart of play and disciplinary sanction?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee awards a direct free kick to Team B and cautions the defender for the reckless challenge. When two offences are committed at the same time, only one yellow card is shown, as the referee punishes the more serious offence. In this case, the physical, reckless foul is  more serious than the tactical offence of stopping a promising attack.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player commits a second cautionable offence in the same match, so the referee shows a second yellow card and a red card to the offender. Any additional sanction/suspension resulting from the offensive language will be decided by the appropriate disciplinary body.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player is serving a temporary dismissal (sin bin) at the end of the second half. The match is drawn and will be followed by penalties (penalty shoot-out). May the referee permit this player to take part? </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Yes, the Laws of the Game protocol allows a temporarily dismissed player to participate in the penalties (penalty shoot-out) even if the full amount of the temporary dismissal period has not elapsed.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>After the first half has ended, a player argues with an opponent and strikes them in the face on the field of play. The referee is informed by another match official about the incident as they are leaving the field, heading to the tunnel. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Law 5 clearly states that the referee has the power to show cards during the half-time interval. The offending player must be shown a red card for violent conduct, be prevented from taking any further part in the match, and cannot be replaced by a substitute. If the red card is not shown on the field of play, the player’s team and the opposing team should be informed and, where appropriate, an announcement made for the spectators before the start of the second half.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player is carelessly fouled in the middle of the field. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>As the anticipated advantage did not materialise because of outside interference, the referee awards the (original) direct free kick from the position of the foul.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender of Team A, who was treated outside the field of play, is ready to continue and re-enters the field without the required permission. When the ball is next out of play, the player of Team A is cautioned (yellow card) for re-entering the field of play without permission and sanctioned for any further offence(s).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender trips an attacker in a reckless manner outside the penalty area. In terms of disciplinary sanction, the referee punishes the more serious offence, so it is a red card for the DOGSO offence, not a yellow card for the reckless foul.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>An attacker passes the ball to a team-mate in an offside position and, immediately after that, is fouled by a defender (reckless tackle outside the penalty area). The referee could not allow play to continue because the attacking team could not benefit from the advantage in this situation as their team-mate was offside.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>At a penalty kick, the goalkeeper has both feet in front of the goal line before the ball is kicked. The goalkeeper makes a save but the ball rebounds from the goalkeeper to an attacking team player who scores a goal. What is the correct decision? </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee plays the advantage for the goalkeeper’s offence and awards the goal. As the penalty kick is not retaken, there is no disciplinary sanction (warning or caution) for the goalkeeper.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>The referee stops play because a player (Team A) lies on the ground and is seriously injured. While the player is being assessed by a doctor, Team B is allowed to make a substitution. After it is completed and before play has restarted, the referee is informed by a match official that the injury is a result of a red card offence committed by the substituted player of Team B. What is the correct decision? </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>As the red card offence occurred before the substitution, the player is sent off and the substitution is cancelled. The injured player can remain on the field of play for/after treatment. If the offence occurred when the ball was in play, play restarts with a direct free kick to Team A (or a penalty kick if it occurred in Team B's penalty area).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender commits a foul challenge within their own penalty area which denies an attacker an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) and endangers the safety of the opponent. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee awards a penalty kick and sends off the defender. When two offences occur at the same time, the more serious offence must be punished. Therefore, it is a red card for serious foul play (not a yellow card for the DOGSO offence that was a challenge for the ball inside the penalty area).</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>During penalties (penalty shoot-out), a coach acts in a provocative manner towards opposing team officials. What is the correct decision?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee may take disciplinary action against team officials who fail to act in a responsible manner during kicks. The coach will be cautioned (yellow card) or sent off (red card) depending on the exact circumstances.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>The goalkeeper is sent off for denying the opponent an obvious goal-scoring opportunity. Before play restarts, the team replaces a player with a substitute goalkeeper; the referee, after a VAR review, changes the red card to a yellow card for stopping a promising attack. May the team cancel the substitution in this case? </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee may change a decision until play has restarted:</p><ul><li><p>the change from a red card to a yellow card is permitted</p></li><li><p>cancelling the substitution is permitted:</p><ul><li><p>within the 'spirit' of the Law and for fairness as it only occurred because of the referee's error.</p></li><li><p>within the letter of the Law as the referee technically changes the decision to allow the substitution.</p></li></ul></li></ul></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>Before the team lists have been submitted, a player spits at an opponent in the pre-match warm-up on the field of play. If it is noticed by the match officials, what is the correct procedure? </h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The offender cannot be named on the team list or play in the match and is reported to the appropriate authority. The number of players and substitutes is not reduced. A red card is not shown as cards may not be shown until the referee enters the field of play at the start of the match.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player takes a free kick and the referee forgets to raise the arm above the head to signal that the kick is indirect. Is it allowed to shorten the half-time interval to complete the game earlier?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>Yes, provided that the referee and both teams agree. The referee may also decide to stop, suspend or abandon the match if the condition of the field, its surrounds or the weather conditions do not allow the game to be continued.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A player is injured as the result of a reckless tackle for which the opponent is cautioned (yellow card). What is the correct decision if the player refuses to leave the field?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The injured player is cautioned (yellow card) and must leave the field on the stretcher or on foot.</p><p></p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>Team A player takes the kick-off and kicks the ball directly into the opponent’s goal. What is the correct decision if a Team B player entered the opponents’ half of the field before the ball was in play?</h2></div></div></button><div class="overflow-hidden " style="height:0px;display:none"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledAnswer-sc-1h0lcry-2 gFhnRB"><div class="List__StyledListWrapper-sc-161jxhq-0 clslqZ"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="bg-lightGray p-4 md:p-6"><p>The referee plays advantage for the offence by Team B and awards the goal.</p></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQnAContainer-sc-1h0lcry-1 bWeDxf bg-white"><div class="container"><div class="border-0 border-b border-navyBlueGray"><button type="button" class="block w-full"><div class="CmsHtmlContentFormats__BaseCmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-0 CmsHtmlContentFormats__CmsHtmlContent-sc-14fwepe-1 iFlAld coSdjN"><div class="QuestionAndAnswer__StyledQuestion-sc-1h0lcry-0 ffyiNl"><h2>A defender (Team A) makes a clearance under pressure from an attacker (Team B) and tries to kick the ball away without looking where other opponents are standing. Unfortunately, the ball hits another attacker (Team B) in the face who is three metres away, inside the defender’s penalty area.
